sources_considered.why: Official Census estimates of the AI use rate among US firms through February 2024.
Official Census trends in AI use by firm size through August 2024.
Microsoft's October 2024 earnings call states Copilot penetration of the Fortune 500.

receipt.public_excerpt: bi-weekly estimates of AI use rate rose from 3.7% to 5.4%, with an expected rate of about 6.6% by early Fall 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: In 2024, only about 5% of US firms reported using any AI to produce goods or services. This supports the claim that adoption was not widespread.

receipt.public_excerpt: The largest size class (250+ employees) exhibits the highest use rate, rising from 5.2% to 7.8% over time

evidence_items.explanation: Even among the largest firms, the Census AI use rate stayed under 8% through August 2024. This supports the claim of limited adoption.

evidence_items.locator: Satya Nadella prepared remarks, Microsoft 365 Copilot section

receipt.public_excerpt: All-up, nearly 70% of the Fortune 500 now use Microsoft 365 Copilot

evidence_items.explanation: Microsoft said that most of the largest US companies used its paid generative AI product, the very product he names. This cuts against 'little to suggest' widespread adoption among big businesses, though seat counts are not given.

receipt.public_excerpt: 65 percent of organisations regularly use Gen AI for at least one business function, up from one-third last year.

evidence_items.explanation: A large 2024 industry survey reported regular generative AI use at most respondents' organizations. That is evidence pointing toward widespread adoption.

receipt.public_excerpt: This year, OpenAI is likely to spend around $4 billion on processing power supplied by Microsoft

evidence_items.explanation: Estimated 2024 inference spending (about $4B) was close to or above OpenAI's estimated revenue of $3.5B to $4.5B, with ChatGPT at about $2B of that. This fits his loss framing but does not measure a loss on each prompt.

unresolved_gaps: No public 2024 source separates ChatGPT's serving cost from its revenue, so the per-prompt loss cannot be confirmed or refuted directly.
The surveys disagree because they measure different populations. Census covers all US firms; Microsoft and McKinsey cover large firms or survey respondents.
